insights.claim: odh-gitops implements a dual-track deployment model: Kustomize+OLM for OpenShift and Helm-only for non-OpenShift Kubernetes, creating two parallel maintenance paths for the same platform.
insights.reasoning: The root kustomization.yaml composes OLM-dependent operator subscriptions and configurations, while the rhai-on-xks-chart bundles dependency operators as Helm sub-charts (sail-operator, rhcl-operator, gateway-api, cert-manager-operator, lws-operator) for environments without OLM. This dual-track approach means platform changes must be propagated to both paths, and feature parity between OpenShift and XKS deployments requires coordinated updates across Kustomize overlays and Helm values.

insights.claim: The XKS chart defaults to secure-by-default gateway configuration with TLS enabled and namespace-scoped route attachment (allowedRoutes.namespaces.from: Same), requiring explicit opt-in for cross-namespace route binding.
insights.reasoning: The default gateway TLS configuration uses a platform-managed internal CA (rhai-ca-issuer ClusterIssuer) and restricts route attachment to the gateway's own namespace. This secure default prevents accidental cross-namespace route attachment but requires operators deploying MaaS (which creates HTTPRoutes in a separate model namespace) to explicitly configure Selector-based route policies, creating a potential deployment friction point documented in the values comments.

insights.claim: The XKS chart supports three cloud targets (Azure, CoreWeave, AWS) with structurally similar but independently configured cloud manager blocks, risking configuration drift between cloud-specific deployments.
insights.reasoning: Each cloud target (azure, coreweave, aws) has its own cloudManager and kubernetesEngine configuration block with similar but not identical dependency management policies. For example, all three manage certManager and gatewayAPI with Managed policy, but lws defaults to Unmanaged across all three. Without a shared base configuration, changes to dependency policies must be replicated across all three blocks, creating a maintenance and drift risk.
